score.name: Gerdau S.A.
score.sector: Industrials / Steel (long & special steel, Brazil & North America)
score.moat_justification: Weak moat, 3/10. Gerdau has real scale advantages - largest long-steel producer in the Americas, scrap-based mini-mill cost position in North America (62% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA), captive iron ore expanding at Miguel Burnier, and a disciplined 0.76x net debt/EBITDA balance sheet - but none of it converts into pricing power or through-cycle returns: gross margin compressed from 26.6% (FY2021) to 22.8% / 16.4% / 13.7% / 11.4% across FY2022-25 and roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) fell from 41.7% (FY2021) to 29.3% / 18.2% / 12.5% / 4.4% over the same years, with FY2016 at -6.7%. A steelmaker whose ROIC only clears its cost of capital at cycle peaks, whose home market is import-capped, and whose product is a global commodity has a weak moat. A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years.

score.one_liner: Americas long-steel scale with a weak commodity moat 3/10 - the normalized base OE of $0.42/share is a mid-cycle construct (FY2025 printed $0.09 on peak capex and crushed Brazil spreads); at $5.08 the weighted IRR is 10.21% by numbers (Tier C), but on each fiscal year's own filed diluted share count the median base is $0.4068/share and the weighted IRR replays to 9.89% - final Tier D via tier_override, IV@15% $3.14 by numbers ($3.01 on the corrected count); on the corrected count it clears 15% only below ~$3.01.
score.exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
score.tier_override_reason: Numbers tier is C at a 10.21% weighted IRR, but that IRR rests on the single-value shares_override: the engine applies the FY2025 total diluted count (2,012,732,574) to every missing year, while the same FY2025 20-F Note 24 table files FY2024's own total diluted count at 2,099,379,471 and FY2023's at 2,109,593,750. On each year's own filed count the 3-yr median base is $0.406841/share (FY2024 OE $854,113,196 / 2,099,379,471; FY2023 $0.551412, FY2025 $0.089379 — FY2024 remains the median year), and replaying the run's unchanged scenario inputs on that base gives a 9.89% weighted IRR and IV@15 of $3.01 — Tier D. A per-year share series is outside the override layer (single-value, fill-only) and a base_override built on the filing's counts is outside the run-outputs bound, so the correction is taken as this quantified tier_override; the by-numbers C at 10.21% remains printed in score.json.
moat_for: Americas long-steel scale: largest long-steel producer in the Americas, 11.6 Mt shipped in 2025 (+5.9%), with integrated scrap-based mini-mills - scrap is the low-cost, flexible feedstock in North America

North America earnings engine: 62% of FY2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA (company 4Q25 release), ~90 days of order backlog and resilient data-center/renewables demand, in a market protected by US trade measures

Vertical integration upstream: captive iron ore (Miguel Burnier expansion, ~R$1.1B potential annual EBITDA at full ramp per the 4Q25 release) and scrap collection lower delivered cost through the cycle

Balance-sheet discipline: FY2025 net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.76x (company release), below the company's own 1.5x policy ceiling, with gross debt of R$14.18B (20-F Notes 15/16: loans and financing R$9.77B + debentures R$4.41B) against equity of R$53.80B in fundamentals.json

Shareholder returns through the trough: FY2025 dividends + buybacks R$2.4B (182.3% of the bylaws payout measure, company release); preferred share count fell from 1,377,906,016 weighted (FY2023) to 1,285,879,767 (FY2025) in the 20-F EPS note
moat_against: Commodity long/special steel: no pricing power - steel prices are set globally and Brazilian prices are capped by imports (import share ~22% of the domestic market in 2025 vs a far lower historical average); gross margin fell from 26.6% (FY2021) to 11.4% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json

Returns are cyclical, not structural: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json swung from -6.7% (FY2016) to 41.7% (FY2021) and back down to 4.4% (FY2025) - a through-cycle record that does not stay above the cost of capital
Scale rivals everywhere: Nucor, Steel Dynamics and Commercial Metals in the US, ArcelorMittal and CSN in Brazil; low-cost import supply (China-origin) disciplines every market Gerdau serves

BRL and Brazil macro exposure: reporting currency BRL converted at period-end rates, Brazilian rates high for prolonged periods, and the controlling family structure (Metalurgica Gerdau) adds a governance layer
Capex intensity is rising into the trough: FY2025 capex $1.251B (R$6.85B incl. intangibles) on the Miguel Burnier mining build, against FY2025 conservative OE of only $179.9M (R$985M)

description.text: The world steel industry is composed of hundreds of steel producing facilities and is divided into two major categories based on the production method utilized: integrated steel mills and non-integrated steel mills, sometimes referred to as “mini mills.” Integrated steel mills normally produce steel from iron oxide, which is extracted from iron ore melted in blast furnaces, and refine the iron into steel, mainly using basic oxygen furnaces or, more rarely, electric arc furnaces. Non-integrated steel mills produce steel by melting in electric arc furnaces scrap steel, which occasionally is complemented by other metals such as direct-reduced iron or hot-compressed iron. According to World Steel, in 2024 (the most recent year for which information is available), 29.3% of the total crude steel production in the world was through electric furnaces (non-integrated process), 70.5% was through basic oxygen furnaces (integrated process) and the remaining 0.3% in other processes.

about.description_short: Gerdau SA produces steel and steel products. The company operates in civil construction, agriculture, automotive, iron ore, exports, research and development, and home steel products sectors. It offers products such as nails, rebar, columns, billets, slabs, tribar tutor, mechanical construction bars, reinforced steel locks. The company's geographical segment includes Brazil Operations; North America Operations; South America Operations as well as Special Steel Operations. It derives most of the revenue from the Brazil Operations segment.

analysis_md:
# GGB — Gerdau S.A.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19 (engine 5.5.0). Brazilian long- and special-steel producer, NYSE ADS (each ADS = one preferred share, ads_ratio 1.0 — see OVERRIDE). Market cap $10.225B at $5.08 (key_numbers.md) — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The largest long-steel producer in the Americas: scrap-based mini-mills and integrated plants in Brazil, North America and South America, plus special steels and captive iron ore. 11.6 Mt shipped in 2025 (+5.9%, company 4Q25 release). North America produced 62% of FY2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA; Brazil is squeezed by record import penetration. A commodity cyclical, priced in BRL at home and as a 1:1 preferred-share ADS in New York.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,458,189,602; capex $1,251,054,653 (rollup: PP&E $1,219,796,547 + intangibles $31,258,106, key_numbers.md capex basis); SBC $27,239,778 (always a real cost, and small here).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $179,895,172 = $0.09/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $0.09; latest FY OE total $179.9M)
- Maintenance version as the engine prints it (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $196,063,034 — but that is not a valid cross-check for FY2025: its ΔNWC (+$62,887,007) differences BRL balance sheets after period-end FX conversion, the same distortion documented under NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE for FY2024. In the reporting currency, noncash working capital fell R$14.050B → R$12.788B in FY2025 (a R$1.262B release); on that basis the maintenance figure recomputes to ~$489M, well above the conservative OE — so the maintenance definition does not corroborate the $179.9M for the latest year, and the conservative figure stands on its own filed legs (OCF − capex − SBC), not on this cross-check.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md), but collapsing: OE totals $1,163,256,045 (FY2023) → $854,113,196 (FY2024) → $179,895,172 (FY2025) in financials_history.csv. The FY2025 crush is mostly cash earnings, not capex: in the reporting currency (fundamentals.json), OCF fell R$11.381B → R$7.987B (−R$3.394B, ~79% of the OE decline) as Brazil spreads were import-crushed, while total capex rose R$5.946B → R$6.853B (+R$0.907B, ~21%) on the Miguel Burnier mining build; the company guides 2026 capex down to R$4.7B (4Q25 release).
- Balance sheet (DEBT_TAGS_BLANK resolution, from the filing): 20-F Notes 15/16 put loans and financing at R$9,774,752 thousand and debentures at R$4,407,399 thousand at December 31, 2025 — gross debt ≈ R$14.18B — against cash of $1,082,429,275 (financials_history.csv, converted) and equity of $9,821,452,152 (financials_history.csv). The company's own leverage measure is net debt/adjusted EBITDA of 0.76x at 4Q25, inside its ≤1.5x policy. The engine carries no net-debt figure for this name (net debt latest: — in key_numbers.md) because no IFRS debt tag it reads is filed; leverage is therefore taken from the filing, not the engine.

**Base used = normalized base, median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $0.42/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; key_numbers.md base OE/share $0.42, normalized OE/share $0.42, latest FY $0.09). No TTM base: Gerdau is an IFRS 20-F filer and ttm.py reads US-GAAP facts only — it exited 3 on this run ("ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact"), so per the worker spec the median base is used and the interim evidence is handled in the STALE_FY resolution below. The median is a mid-cycle construct, not a current run-rate — see BASE_DIVERGENCE and the scenario multipliers, which are set against it deliberately.

## OVERRIDES — shares (filing) and ads_ratio
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:shares`. EDGAR companyfacts carries no diluted share count for FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025; the only filed counts are dei outstanding counts for the COMMON class alone (717,782,619 at December 31, 2025), while the 20-F cover states 717,782,619 common shares **and** 1,283,097,330 preferred shares issued. The zero-fill baseline on that common-only count printed a base OE/share of $1.19 and a weighted IRR of 21.09% (key_numbers.md measured impact) — a fake near-A tier built on a third of the capital.
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `shares_override = {value: 2012732574, kind: "filing"}` — the FY2025 20-F EPS note's total diluted denominator: common shares outstanding 718,139,434 + preferred diluted total 1,294,593,140 (weighted-average preferred 1,285,879,767 + 8,713,373 potential shares from long-term incentive plans). This is the matching denominator for consolidated owner's earnings because the EPS note allocates earnings identically per share to both classes (diluted EPS R$0.69 / R$2.18 / R$3.56 for common **and** preferred, FY2025/24/23) and the traded ADS is itself a preferred share. It is not a share_class_mismatch: the EPS note presents EPS for the traded class itself, on the same per-share economics as the common.
- **Known approximation, disclosed:** the engine applies the single value to every period with no filed diluted count (key_numbers.md lists periods filled 2016-12-31 through 2025-12-31). FY2025 is exact. FY2024 OE/share is computed on 2,012,732,574 instead of its own filed total of 2,099,379,471 (overstates FY2024 OE/share by ~4.3%) and FY2023 on 2,012,732,574 instead of 2,109,593,750 (~4.8% overstatement) — the direction makes the median base slightly generous, not conservative. The pre-2023 years are outside the median window; their per-share history is approximate on any basis (see SHARES_FALLBACK).
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md / score.json override_impact):** base OE/share $1.19 (no override) → $0.42 (with override), −64.23%; weighted IRR 21.09% → 10.21% (−10.89pp). Unblocks tier: YES — without it the filing gap blocks scoring entirely. Because the tier exists only because of this override, both alert gates are closed (score.json exit_alert_suppressed_reason: "tier exists only because of a judgment override").
- **ads_ratio:** judgment.json declares `{ratio: 1.0}` from the same 20-F: the NYSE Level II ADSs are equivalent to one preferred share (GGBR4). No scaling applies; the declaration exists so the ADS price and the per-share figures are confirmed on the same unit.
- **Tier correction taken on this override (tier_override → D, added in PR review):** the approximation above is load-bearing for the tier label. On each fiscal year's own filed diluted count from the same Note 24 table, the 3-yr median base is $0.406841/share (FY2024 OE $854,113,196 ÷ 2,099,379,471; FY2023 $0.551412 on 2,109,593,750; FY2025 $0.089379; FY2024 remains the median year), and replaying this run's unchanged scenario inputs on that base gives a weighted IRR of 9.89% and IV@15 of $3.01 — Tier D, not C. A per-year share series is outside the override layer (single-value, fill-only) and a base_override built on the filing's counts is outside the run-outputs bound, so the correction is recorded as a quantified `tier_override` in judgment.json: **final tier D**, with the by-numbers C at 10.21% still printed in score.json.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: scale without pricing power. Gross margin (fundamentals.json) compressed from 26.6% (FY2021) to 22.8% / 16.4% / 13.7% / 11.4% across FY2022–25, and roic_proxy fell from 41.7% (FY2021) to 29.3% / 18.2% / 12.5% / 4.4% over the same years after printing −6.7% in FY2016 — returns clear the cost of capital only at cycle peaks.
- FOR: largest long-steel producer in the Americas (11.6 Mt shipped 2025, +5.9%) with a scrap-based mini-mill cost position; North America is 62% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA with ~90 days of backlog and trade-measure shelter; captive iron ore (Miguel Burnier, ~R$1.1B potential annual EBITDA at full ramp per the 4Q25 release) lowers delivered cost; disciplined balance sheet (0.76x net debt/EBITDA vs a ≤1.5x policy) and R$2.4B returned in FY2025 dividends + buybacks, with the preferred count bought down from 1,377,906,016 weighted (FY2023) to 1,285,879,767 (FY2025).
- AGAINST: commodity product with prices set globally and Brazilian prices capped by imports (~22% import share of the domestic market in 2025); ROIC and gross margin both in a four-year slide; scale rivals on both continents (Nucor, Steel Dynamics, ArcelorMittal, CSN) plus low-cost import supply; BRL/Brazil macro exposure and a family control layer (Metalúrgica Gerdau); capex intensity rising into the trough (FY2025 capex $1,251.1M against OE of $179.9M).
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended start is g_base 1.07% (components, key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 8.62%, rev CAGR 3y −6.47%, latest rev YoY 17.68%, OE/share CAGR 2y −60.65%). The +17.68% latest YoY is a USD figure flattered by BRL appreciation at period-end FX rates; in the reporting currency FY2025 revenue grew +4.2% (R$69,858,532 thousand vs R$67,026,656 thousand, fundamentals.json) on shipments +5.9%. A ~1% base start sits in line with the BRL prints and below the FX-flattered USD print — that gap is the written reason. Bull +6.1% requires a genuine spread recovery (North America momentum plus Miguel Burnier ramp); super-bull +13.1% requires a 2021-style price spike and is weighted at only 8%.

Scenario calibration against the base: the median base ($0.42) embeds FY2023–24 spreads that no longer exist (FY2025 printed $0.09), so the default bear multipliers (0.90 / 0.75) would still leave even the super-bear case at ~3.5x the latest FY print. Multipliers were therefore set to 0.60 / 0.85 / 1.00 / 1.10 / 1.25 so the bear cases cut well below the median base, and probabilities tilted bear-ward (15/30/30/17/8 = 45% on bear-or-worse) for a cyclical at a spread trough with peak capex. One calibration limit, stated plainly: even the super-bear path bottoms at ~$0.17/share (year 6 of the stored path in dcf_numbers.json), roughly 1.9x the FY2025 print of $0.09 — no scenario is calibrated to reach the FY2025 print itself, because that print is treated as a peak-capex distortion rather than a run-rate floor (see BASE_DIVERGENCE). If FY2025's capex intensity persisted, outcomes would be worse than the super-bear path shows. Price $5.08.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -10.0% | 0.60 | Brazil import crush deepens; NA fades; trough spreads persist | $1.33 | 5.51% |
| Bear | 30% | -3.9% | 0.85 | Trough spreads persist; OE stays well below the median base | $2.35 | 8.13% |
| Base | 30% | 1.1% | 1.00 | Median base holds; capex normalizes toward the R$4.7B guide | $3.31 | 10.61% |
| Bull | 17% | 6.1% | 1.10 | NA strength + Miguel Burnier ramp restore spreads | $4.33 | 13.20% |
| Super bull | 8% | 13.1% | 1.25 | 2021-style price spike | $6.25 | 17.67% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $3.14 (−38.3% vs price), IV@12% $4.12, IV@10% $5.22, weighted IRR 10.21%, base-case IRR 10.61%** (key_numbers.md)
- **Tier by numbers: C. Final tier: D** via the quantified tier_override recorded in the OVERRIDES section (per-year filed share counts: median base $0.4068/share, weighted IRR replays to 9.89%, IV@15 $3.01). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 8.35%, terminal value 17.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.69x, 9.6 months since FY end. Hurdle-clearing prices on the weighted path: 15% at $3.14, 20% at $2.24, 25% at $1.75.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): no TTM base is available — ttm.py exited 3 because it reads US-GAAP facts only and Gerdau is an IFRS 20-F filer; the median base is used per spec. Interim evidence (6-K releases) cuts both ways and is not pinned: Q2 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of R$3.4B was the strongest since Q3 2023 on North America (shipments +7% YoY, EBITDA +15% QoQ), with positive quarterly free cash flow — a recovery from the FY2025 trough is under way, but FY2026 capex is still guided at R$4.7B, so interim OE remains well below the median base; that is priced through the bear-tilted weights, not a TTM pin.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $0.09 vs median $0.42): neither figure is an error — the latest FY is the distorted one as a run-rate (trough Brazil spreads cut OCF by R$3.394B in BRL, ~79% of the OE decline, with peak Miguel Burnier capex adding R$0.907B, ~21%), and the median is generous as a run-rate (it embeds FY2023–24 spreads). The base kept is the median, with the distortion handled explicitly: bear/super-bear OE multipliers of 0.85 / 0.60 and 45% weight on bear-or-worse. Anyone quoting the $0.42 base without that adjustment is overstating current earnings power.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares**: see OVERRIDES — gap, construction, approximation and measured impact (−64.23% on the base, −10.89pp on weighted IRR, unblocks the tier) are all recorded in fields (judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json overrides_applied/override_impact, overrides_registry.json), not just here.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: ratio 1.0 declared from the filer's own 20-F (each ADS = one preferred share); per-share figures and the $5.08 ADS price are on the same unit, so no scaling distorts the result.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: the >60% revenue jump is FY2021 (R$43,814,661 thousand → R$78,345,081 thousand in fundamentals.json, +78.8%) — the post-COVID global steel price spike, not a divestiture, acquisition or restatement (the small 2025 deals — Gerdau Summit buy-in, Kloeckner Metals Brasil — are immaterial to the revenue base). Growth inputs do not straddle it: the blend's median leans on the 3-yr CAGR (−6.47%) and the scenario starts were sanity-checked against BRL prints, not the spike-era 5-yr CAGR (8.62%).
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real cyclicality, not noise — this is a steel spread cycle (OE/share $0.58 → $0.42 → $0.09 across FY2023–25 on the override count, financials_history.csv). Handled by the normalized median base, 45% bear-or-worse probability weight, and trough-spanning bear multipliers.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025): FY2025's gap is named — R$2.0B of non-cash asset impairment losses in Brazilian units (company 4Q25 release/call) cut net income without touching operating cash flow; adjusted net income for FY2025 was R$3.4B, down 21%. In both years depreciation & amortisation is structurally large against net income in this capital base (D&A $672,475,278 in FY2025, financials_history.csv). FY2024 reconciled in the reporting currency (fundamentals.json, BRL): OCF R$11.381B − NI R$4.599B = a R$6.782B gap, of which D&A R$3.126B plus a noncash working-capital release of R$858M (balance-sheet NCWC R$14.908B → R$14.050B) explains R$3.984B; the remaining ~R$2.80B sits in NI-side non-cash and other items not separately broken out in this folder's outputs. The engine's delta_nwc (−$800,543,861) overstates the release roughly 5.6x — it differences BRL balance sheets after period-end FX conversion, so the BRL release is ≈$143M, not $800M. Base relevance: the only one-off inside OCF itself is that R$858M release (~17% of FY2024 OE total); stripping it lowers FY2024 OE/share on the corrected per-year count to ~$0.34 — still the median year, and it pushes the base down, not up. The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is unaffected by the impairment (non-cash). (The engine's maintenance variant is not a corroboration for FY2025 — its FX-distorted ΔNWC buries the R$1.262B working-capital release; on a BRL basis it prints ~$489M, above the conservative figure. See Owner's earnings.)
- **FX_CONVERTED**: reporting currency BRL converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (rates recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion; FY2025 at 0.18256). Flow facts use period-end, not average, rates — one more reason the USD revenue YoY (+17.68%) overstates underlying growth vs the BRL print (+4.2%); scenario starts were set off the BRL evidence.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2016–2022): those history years' per-share figures are approximate on any basis — the originally filed counts are class-dimensioned or basic-only, and the final CSV carries the shares_override count (periods filled listed in key_numbers.md). None of 2016–2022 is in the 3-yr median window; the only blend input touching them is the 5-yr revenue CAGR, which is share-count-independent.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: resolved in the Owner's earnings section above from the filing itself — gross debt ≈ R$14.18B (loans and financing R$9,774,752 thousand + debentures R$4,407,399 thousand, 20-F Notes 15/16), company-reported net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.76x. Net debt is unknown to the engine, not zero; no engine leverage verdict is claimed.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.69x): real — a trough cyclical's outcome range is this wide. Confidence is capped at low, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 8.13% vs bull tier C at 13.20%): sized to the bear end — even the bull case does not clear 15%, so the band disagreement does not change the investment conclusion, only the C/D label.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the base, not the tier: on the filed common-only share count this name screens as a fake 21.09% weighted IRR; on the correct consolidated diluted count it is a 10.21% weighted IRR whose base ($0.42) is itself a mid-cycle construct sitting 4.7x above the latest FY print ($0.09) — and on each year's own filed diluted count the same median construction gives $0.4068/share and a 9.89% weighted IRR (Tier D), which is the basis of the final tier. Method range across defensible bases runs from clear-D (latest-FY base) through D (per-year filed counts) to the printed by-numbers C (single-count median base with bear-tilted scenarios).
- What would have to go right: capex actually falling to the R$4.7B 2026 guide, Miguel Burnier delivering its ~R$1.1B EBITDA potential, North America holding its 62%-of-EBITDA form, and Brazilian trade defense biting on imports. Q2 2026 (adjusted EBITDA R$3.4B, strongest since Q3 2023) is the first print consistent with that path — one quarter, not a trend.
- Quality is not the debate: OE was positive 5 of the last 5 years, SBC is negligible ($27.2M), leverage is 0.76x on the company's measure, and the buyback is shrinking the preferred count. The debate is purely what a normalized steel spread is worth — and at $5.08 the market is already paying for a good part of the recovery (price is 62% above the weighted IV@15% of $3.14 and above even the base-case IV@15% of $3.31).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** — C by numbers (weighted IRR 10.21% on the single FY2025 share count), taken down by the quantified tier_override in the OVERRIDES section: on each year's own filed diluted count the median base is $0.4068/share and the weighted IRR replays to 9.89%; the bear end is D at 8.13% on either basis, and the verdict is sized there
- Confidence: **Low** (WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD 4.69x, TIER_BAND spanning D–C, a median base 4.7x the latest print, and a tier that exists only because of a filing override)
